newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Shum Yip offers 250 mln shrs at HK$1.85 each.
newsitem.headline: HK's Shum Yip offers 250 mln shrs at HK$1.85 each.

text.p: Shenzhen municipal government backed Shum Yip Investment Ltd said on Thursday it is offering 250 million shares at HK$1.85 per share in its flotation.
Some 175 million will be placed internationally, while 75 million shares will be offered to the public in Hong Kong.
The company has also granted underwriters an over-allotment option to issue an additional 37.5 million shares.

The shares have a price/earnings (P/E) ratio of 10.6 times on a fully diluted basis, and their discount to net asset value per share is about 10 percent. The company's adjusted tangible net asset value per share is HK$2.06.
The company estimated a proforma net profit for the year ended December 31, 1996, of not less than HK$155 million.
The Hong Kong public offer will run from February 21 to 26 and dealing in shares is expected to begin on March 7.
Peregrine Capital Ltd is the global coordinator, sponsor and lead manager of the issue.
After the listing, Shum Yim Investment's parent, Shum Yip Holdings Co ltd, will hold 63 percent of the company.

Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd will hold 3.5 percent, a subsidiary of Peregrine Investments Holdings Ltd will hold three percent, and 2.5 percent, two percent and one percent will be held by KP Choi Ltd, the Tai Ping Life Insurance Co Ltd, and Conch Development Ltd respectively.

Shum Yip engages in property development and investment primarily in Shenzhen, across the border in China from Hong Kong. It also engages in the provision of transportation services in China and between Hong Kong and China.

The company's parent acts as the trading and investment vehicle for Shenzhen Municipal Government in Hong Kong, and is a representative organisation to establish economics links between Shenzhen and overseas investors.

"Shum Yip is the flagship listed vehicle of the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government in accessing the international capital market. We will fully support its future development," Wu Jiesi, the vice mayor of Shenzhen, said in a statement.

The company said of net proceeds of HK$434 million before the excercise of the over-allotment option, HK$90 million will be used to develop intercity coach services in China and HK$60 million for to develop a nationwide car rental business.
The balance will be used to finance its existing property development projects and as general working capital.
